\section{Space Complexity --- Savitch ARM --- Deepen}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.SpaceComplexity.SavitchARM.Deepen
This module builds a register machine that decides any language accepted by a
nondeterministic machine in space $\mathit{sp}$ without computing $\mathit{sp}$: for radii
$s=1,2,\dots$ it runs Savitch's midpoint-reachability search once to test whether a configuration
touching the edge of the radius-$s$ window is reachable, and, once none is, runs the search again to
decide acceptance. Its registers stay within $O\bigl((\mathit{sp}(|x|)+\log|x|+1)^2\bigr)$ binary
digits, which is the hypothesis used to derive Savitch's theorem for every space bound at least
logarithmic.

\begin{definition}[Contract of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DeepenContract}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DeepenContract}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LOGSPACE, Complexity.LogProg.AHalt, Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.logSpace, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
For a language $L\subseteq\{0,1\}^*$ and a function $\mathit{sp}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, the
deepening contract for $L$ and $\mathit{sp}$ is the proposition that there exist $m,d\in\mathbb{N}$,
a finite label set $\Lambda$ with decidable equality, an abstract register machine $D$ with $m$
registers, $d$ deciders and labels $\Lambda$, a start label $l_0\in\Lambda$, languages
$A_0,\dots,A_{d-1}$ all in $\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{SPACE}(\lambda)$, and a constant $C\in\mathbb{N}$, such that
for every input $x\in\{0,1\}^*$ the machine $D$, run on $x$ with the indicator functions of the
$A_j$ as oracles from label $l_0$ with every register $0$, halts with answer $[x\in L]$ along a run in
which every configuration before halting satisfies the syntactic preconditions of its instruction
and every register value $r$ satisfies
$|\mathrm{bin}(r+1)|\le C\,(\mathit{sp}(|x|)+\lambda(|x|)+1)^2$. Here
$\lambda(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$ (with $\lambda(0)=1$) and $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ is the binary
representation of $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Labels of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Lb}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$, the label set $\Lambda_c$ of the iterative-deepening machine is the finite set
consisting of: two copies of the labels of Savitch's search machine, one for the edge block and one
for the accept block; seven setup labels (an input-length scan, its increment, an increment of the
length-of-length counter, a zero test, a halving step, a second counter increment, and setting the
radius to $1$); for each block flag $f\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ the block-preparation
labels, namely $21$ register-clear labels, seven phases for each of the copy loops (radius into the
sum, counter into the sum, $c$ width copies indexed by $i<c$, radius into the block, width into the
block, width into the shift counter), nine phases of the shift loop, and single labels for one sum
increment, clearing the block's width, clearing and then setting the block's code bound to $1$, and
clearing the block's three node registers; a next-radius label; and an answer label for each bit
$b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Block register inclusion]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ}
\leanok
The map $\rho:\{0,\dots,17\}\to\{0,\dots,24\}$ is the inclusion $\rho(r)=r$; it identifies the $18$
registers of Savitch's search block with the first $18$ of the $25$ registers of the
iterative-deepening machine.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Injectivity of the block register inclusion]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ_inj}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ_inj}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ}
\difficulty{1}
The inclusion $\rho:\{0,\dots,17\}\to\{0,\dots,24\}$, $\rho(r)=r$, is injective.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Own registers avoid the block]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ_ne}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ_ne}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\rho:\{0,\dots,17\}\to\{0,\dots,24\}$ be the inclusion $\rho(r)=r$. For every
$r\in\{0,\dots,17\}$ and every $r'\in\{0,\dots,24\}$ with $r'\ge 18$, we have $\rho(r)\ne r'$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Copy loop of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCopyI}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCopyI}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
Let $c\in\mathbb{N}$, let $a,b\in\{0,\dots,24\}$ be registers, let $e\in\Lambda_c$ be an exit label
and let $k_0,\dots,k_6\in\Lambda_c$ be labels. The copy loop is the family of seven instructions
indexed by $j\in\{0,\dots,6\}$: ($0$) if register $a$ is zero go to $k_4$, else to $k_1$; ($1$)
decrement $a$ and go to $k_2$; ($2$) increment $b$ and go to $k_3$; ($3$) increment the scratch
register $24$ and go to $k_0$; ($4$) if register $24$ is zero exit to $e$, else go to $k_5$; ($5$)
decrement register $24$ and go to $k_6$; ($6$) increment $a$ and go to $k_4$. Placed at the labels
$k_j$, it is designed to add the value of $a$ to $b$, restoring $a$ through register $24$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Shift loop of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpShlI}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpShlI}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.Ins, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rK}
Let $c\in\mathbb{N}$, let $e\in\Lambda_c$ be an exit label and let $k_0,\dots,k_8\in\Lambda_c$ be
labels. Writing $K=9$ for the code-bound register of the search block, the shift loop is the family
of nine instructions indexed by $j\in\{0,\dots,8\}$: ($0$) if register $20$ is zero exit to $e$,
else go to $k_1$; ($1$) decrement register $20$, go to $k_2$; ($2$) if register $K$ is zero go to
$k_6$, else to $k_3$; ($3$) decrement $K$, go to $k_4$; ($4$) increment register $24$, go to $k_5$;
($5$) increment register $24$, go to $k_2$; ($6$) if register $24$ is zero go to $k_0$, else to
$k_7$; ($7$) decrement register $24$, go to $k_8$; ($8$) increment $K$, go to $k_6$. Each round
doubles $K$ and decrements register $20$, so the loop is designed to multiply $K$ by $2$ raised to
the initial value of register $20$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Successor of a register clear]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCbEx}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCbEx}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$, a block flag $f$ and $i\in\{0,\dots,20\}$, the successor label of the $i$-th
register clear of block preparation $f$ in $\Lambda_c$ is the $(i+1)$-th register-clear label of
preparation $f$ if $i+1<21$, and otherwise phase $0$ of the copy loop of preparation $f$ that adds
the radius to the sum register.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Successor of a width copy]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCtEx}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCtEx}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$, a block flag $f$ and $i<c$, the successor label of the $i$-th width copy of
block preparation $f$ in $\Lambda_c$ is phase $0$ of the $(i+1)$-th width copy if $i+1<c$, and
otherwise phase $0$ of the copy loop of preparation $f$ that writes the radius into the search
block.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[First width copy]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCt0}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCt0}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$ and a block flag $f$, the first width-copy label of block preparation $f$ in
$\Lambda_c$ is phase $0$ of the $0$-th width copy if $c>0$, and otherwise phase $0$ of the copy
loop of preparation $f$ that writes the radius into the search block.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Entry label of a search block]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpIn}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpIn}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$ and a block flag $f$, the entry label of block $f$ in $\Lambda_c$ is the
outer-search entry label of Savitch's search machine in the edge-block copy when $f$ is false, and
in the accept-block copy when $f$ is true.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Exits of the edge block]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpkE}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpkE}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$, the exit map of the edge block sends a bit $b$ to a label of $\Lambda_c$: the
next-radius label if $b$ is true (an edge code is reachable), and the first register-clear label of
the accept block's preparation if $b$ is false.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decider rerouting of the edge block]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpσE}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpσE}
\leanok
The map $\sigma_E:\{0,1,2,3\}\to\{0,1,2,3,4\}$ is given by $\sigma_E(0)=0$, $\sigma_E(1)=1$,
$\sigma_E(2)=4$ and $\sigma_E(3)=3$; it makes the search's accepting-code decider read the
edge-code decider instead.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Decider rerouting of the accept block]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpσA}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpσA}
\leanok
The map $\sigma_A:\{0,1,2,3\}\to\{0,1,2,3,4\}$ is the inclusion $\sigma_A(j)=j$ for
$j\in\{0,1,2,3\}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Iterative-deepening register machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpD}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpD}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.ARM, Complexity.LogProg.Ins.embed, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.A, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCbEx, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCopyI, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCt0, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpCtEx, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpIn, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpShlI, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpkE, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpσA, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpσE, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rK, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rM, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rU, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rV, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rs, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rw}
For $c\in\mathbb{N}$, the iterative-deepening machine $D_c$ is the abstract register machine with
$25$ registers, $5$ deciders and label set $\Lambda_c$ defined as follows. On the edge-block labels
it runs Savitch's search machine with registers included by $\rho(r)=r$, deciders rerouted by
$\sigma_E=(0,1,4,3)$, and an answer $b$ replaced by a jump (testing register $24$) to the next-radius
label if $b$ is true or to the accept block's preparation if $b$ is false; on the accept-block
labels it runs the same search with deciders rerouted by $\sigma_A=(0,1,2,3)$ and answers $b$
replaced by jumps to the answer label for $b$. The setup counts $|x|$ into register $21$ by
repeatedly querying decider $0$ and incrementing, sets register $22$ to $1$, halves register $21$
down to $0$ while incrementing register $22$ each time, and increments the radius register $23$
before entering the edge block's preparation. The preparation of block $f$ clears registers
$0,\dots,20$, sets register $18$ to $s+\ell+1$ (radius $s$ in register $23$, $\ell$ in register
$22$), adds register $18$ to register $19$ $c$ times, copies the radius into the block's radius
register $7$ and register $19$ into the block's width register $8$, sets the block's code bound
register $9$ to $1$, copies register $19$ into register $20$, runs the shift loop, clears the block's
registers $10$, $11$, $12$, and enters block $f$. The next-radius label increments register $23$ and
returns to the edge block's preparation, and the answer label for $b$ halts with answer $b$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Deciders of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpAs}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpAs}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.acceptLang, Complexity.Codec.edgeLang, Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.Codec.stepLang, Complexity.inputLenLang, Turing.FinNDTM}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean alphabet, the five decider languages
$A_0,\dots,A_4$ are: $A_0$ the input-length language
$\{\langle u,\mathrm{bin}(i)\rangle : i<|u|\}$; $A_1$ the initial-code language of $N$; $A_2$ the
accepting-code language of $N$; $A_3$ the step-pair language of $N$; and $A_4$ the edge-code
language of $N$ (codes at radius $s$ of window-bounded configurations with some work head at
position $\pm s$).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Oracle answers of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpOrc}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpOrc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpAs, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.MultiTapeTM.indicator}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean alphabet, the oracle family is the
map sending $j\in\{0,\dots,4\}$ and a word $V\in\{0,1\}^*$ to the indicator $[V\in A_j]$, where
$A_0,\dots,A_4$ are the input-length, initial-code, accepting-code, step-pair and edge-code
languages of $N$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Oracle answer is membership]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_mem}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_mem}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpAs, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpOrc, Complexity.LogProg.indicator_eq_decide, Turing.FinNDTM}
\difficulty{2}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet, and let
$A_0,\dots,A_4$ be its input-length, initial-code, accepting-code, step-pair and edge-code
languages. For every $j\in\{0,\dots,4\}$ and every word $V$, the oracle answer $[V\in A_j]$ is true
if and only if $V\in A_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rerouted oracle step relation]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_rel}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_rel}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.StepRel, Complexity.Codec.stepRel_iff_mem, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.Rel, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpOrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_mem, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.rel_iff_orc, Turing.FinNDTM}
\difficulty{3}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet, let
$\sigma:\{0,1,2,3\}\to\{0,\dots,4\}$ satisfy $\sigma(3)=3$, let $x\in\{0,1\}^*$ and $s\in\mathbb{N}$.
Then for all $u,v\in\mathbb{N}$, decider $\sigma(3)$ of $N$'s five-language oracle family accepts
$\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bin}(u),\langle\mathrm{bin}(v),\mathrm{bin}(s)\rangle\rangle\rangle$ if and
only if $u,v$ are related by the step relation of $N$ on $x$ at radius $s$, i.e.\ that encoding lies
in the step-pair language of $N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rerouted initial-code test]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_initO}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_initO}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.initLang, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.InitO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpOrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_mem, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.initO_iff_orc, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{2}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet, let
$\sigma:\{0,1,2,3\}\to\{0,\dots,4\}$ satisfy $\sigma(1)=1$, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^*$ and
$s,u\in\mathbb{N}$. Decider $\sigma(1)$ of $N$'s five-language oracle family accepts
$\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bin}(u),\mathrm{bin}(s)\rangle\rangle$ if and only if that word lies in the
initial-code language of $N$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Rerouted accepting-code test]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_accO}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_accO}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.AccO, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.accO_iff_orc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpAs, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpOrc, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_mem, Turing.FinNDTM, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet with decider languages
$A_0,\dots,A_4$, let $\sigma:\{0,1,2,3\}\to\{0,\dots,4\}$ and $j\in\{0,\dots,4\}$ with
$\sigma(2)=j$, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^*$ and $s,v\in\mathbb{N}$. Decider $\sigma(2)$ of the oracle
family accepts $\langle x,\langle\mathrm{bin}(v),\mathrm{bin}(s)\rangle\rangle$ if and only if that
word lies in $A_j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Preconditions of simple instructions]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_pre}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_pre}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.PreS, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpD, Complexity.LogProg.preS_of_ins}
\difficulty{3}
Let $c\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be an input, let $l\in\Lambda_c$ be a label and $v$ a register
assignment, and consider the iterative-deepening register machine $D_c$ (with $25$ registers, $5$ deciders and $c$ copies of the width step). If the instruction of $D_c$ at $l$ is an increment, a clear or an
answer instruction, then the configuration at label $l$ with registers $v$ and no answer yet
satisfies the syntactic preconditions of $D_c$ on $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Increment step of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_inc}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_inc}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.refl, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.step, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpD, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_pre, Complexity.LogProg.astep_inc}
\difficulty{2}
Let $c,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $o$ be an oracle family for five deciders, let $x$ be an input, and
consider the iterative-deepening register machine $D_c$ (with $25$ registers, $5$ deciders and $c$ copies of the width step). If the instruction of $D_c$ at label $l$ increments register $r$ and continues at
$l'$, and every register of $v$ is at most $B$, then there is a run of $D_c$ on $x$ with oracle family $o$ all of whose configurations before the last satisfy the syntactic preconditions of their instructions and have every register at most $B$ from label $l$ with registers
$v$ to label $l'$ with registers $v[r\mapsto v(r)+1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Clear step of the deepening machine]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_clr}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_clr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.AReach, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.refl, Complexity.LogProg.AReach.step, Complexity.LogProg.GuardLe, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.DpLb, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpD, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dp_pre, Complexity.LogProg.astep_clr}
\difficulty{2}
Let $c,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $o$ be an oracle family for five deciders, let $x$ be an input, and
consider the iterative-deepening register machine $D_c$ (with $25$ registers, $5$ deciders and $c$ copies of the width step). If the instruction of $D_c$ at label $l$ clears register $r$ and continues at $l'$,
and every register of $v$ is at most $B$, then there is a run of $D_c$ on $x$ with oracle family $o$ all of whose configurations before the last satisfy the syntactic preconditions of their instructions and have every register at most $B$ from label $l$ with registers $v$ to
label $l'$ with registers $v[r\mapsto 0]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Split register file]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt}
\leanok
For $b:\{0,\dots,17\}\to\mathbb{N}$ and $o:\{0,\dots,6\}\to\mathbb{N}$, the register file
$\mathrm{St}(b,o):\{0,\dots,24\}\to\mathbb{N}$ assigns $b(r)$ to each register $r<18$ and
$o(r-18)$ to each register $r\ge 18$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Split register file on block registers]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt_ρ}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt_ρ}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ}
\difficulty{3}
For $b:\{0,\dots,17\}\to\mathbb{N}$ and $o:\{0,\dots,6\}\to\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{St}(b,o)$ be
the register file on $\{0,\dots,24\}$ equal to $b$ below $18$ and to $o(\cdot-18)$ from $18$ on,
and let $\rho(r)=r$ include $\{0,\dots,17\}$ into $\{0,\dots,24\}$. Then
$\mathrm{St}(b,o)(\rho(r))=b(r)$ for every $r\in\{0,\dots,17\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Split register file on own registers]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt_own}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt_own}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt}
\difficulty{3}
For $b:\{0,\dots,17\}\to\mathbb{N}$ and $o:\{0,\dots,6\}\to\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{St}(b,o)$ be
the register file on $\{0,\dots,24\}$ equal to $b$ below $18$ and to $o(\cdot-18)$ from $18$ on.
If $r\in\{0,\dots,24\}$ and $i\in\{0,\dots,6\}$ satisfy $r=18+i$, then $\mathrm{St}(b,o)(r)=o(i)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Updating a block register]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt_upd_ρ}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt_upd_ρ}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt, Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpρ}
\difficulty{4}
For $b:\{0,\dots,17\}\to\mathbb{N}$ and $o:\{0,\dots,6\}\to\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{St}(b,o)$ be
the register file on $\{0,\dots,24\}$ equal to $b$ below $18$ and to $o(\cdot-18)$ from $18$ on,
and let $\rho(r)=r$. For every $r\in\{0,\dots,17\}$ and $a\in\mathbb{N}$, updating
$\mathrm{St}(b,o)$ at register $\rho(r)$ to the value $a$ gives $\mathrm{St}(b[r\mapsto a],o)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Updating an own register]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt_upd_own}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt_upd_own}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpSt}
\difficulty{4}
For $b:\{0,\dots,17\}\to\mathbb{N}$ and $o:\{0,\dots,6\}\to\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{St}(b,o)$ be
the register file on $\{0,\dots,24\}$ equal to $b$ below $18$ and to $o(\cdot-18)$ from $18$ on. If
$r\in\{0,\dots,24\}$ and $i\in\{0,\dots,6\}$ satisfy $r=18+i$, then for every $a\in\mathbb{N}$,
updating $\mathrm{St}(b,o)$ at register $r$ to $a$ gives $\mathrm{St}(b,o[i\mapsto a])$.
\end{theorem}

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Largest code width of the deepening run]
\lean{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpW}
\label{Complexity.LogProg.SavitchARM.dpW}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Codec.codeK, Turing.FinNDTM}
For a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ with Boolean alphabet and code-length constant
$k_N$, a function $\mathit{sp}:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$ and an input $x$, the largest code width is
$W=(k_N+1)\bigl(\mathit{sp}(|x|)+1+(1+|\mathrm{bin}(|x|)|)+1\bigr)$, where $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ is the
binary representation of $n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Iterative-deepening loop]

\difficulty{6}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet that decides $L$ in space $\mathit{sp}$ (on every input $x$ every computation branch halts and visits at most $\mathit{sp}(|x|)$ work-tape cells, and $x\in L$ iff some branch accepts), and let
$x$ be an input, where $k_N$ is the code-length constant of $N$, $W=(k_N+1)\bigl(\mathit{sp}(|x|)+1+(1+|\mathrm{bin}(|x|)|)+1\bigr)$, and $D_{k_N+1}$ is the iterative-deepening register machine ($25$ registers, $5$ deciders, $k_N+1$ copies of the width step) run with the oracle family answering membership in the five decider languages of $N$ (input length, initial codes, accepting codes, step pairs and edge codes). For all $k,s\in\mathbb{N}$ with $\mathit{sp}(|x|)+1-s=k$ and
$1\le s\le\mathit{sp}(|x|)+1$, and every register assignment $v$ with
$v(22)=1+|\mathrm{bin}(|x|)|$, $v(23)=s$, $v(24)=0$ and all registers at most $2^{W\cdot W}$,
the machine $D_{k_N+1}$ on $x$, started at the first register-clear label of the edge block's
preparation with registers $v$, halts with answer $[x\in L]$ along a run whose configurations
before halting satisfy the syntactic preconditions and have all registers at most $2^{W\cdot W}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{5}
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean alphabet that decides $L$ in space $\mathit{sp}$ (on every input $x$ every computation branch halts and visits at most $\mathit{sp}(|x|)$ work-tape cells, and $x\in L$ iff some branch accepts). Then there
exist an abstract register machine $D$ with finitely many labels, a start label $l_0$, finitely many
decider languages all in $\mathrm{L}=\mathrm{SPACE}(\lambda)$, and a constant $C\in\mathbb{N}$
such that for every input $x$, the machine $D$ run on $x$ with the indicators of those languages as
oracles, from $l_0$ with every register $0$, halts with answer $[x\in L]$ along a run in which every
configuration before halting satisfies the syntactic preconditions of its instruction and every
register value $r$ satisfies $|\mathrm{bin}(r+1)|\le C\,(\mathit{sp}(|x|)+\lambda(|x|)+1)^2$;
here $\lambda(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1$ and $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ is the binary representation of
$n$. One may take as deciders the input-length, initial-code, accepting-code, step-pair and edge-code
languages of $N$, and $C=9(k_N+1)^2+2$ with $k_N$ the code-length constant of $N$.
\end{theorem}
